facts.text: I have been noticing unusual writing on the wall.
It started yesterday.

facts.item: writing on the wall: what it says
facts.text: It's not clear, and I can't read it most of the time.

facts.item: writing on the wall: what you think it means
facts.text: I think I might be getting instructions from it.

facts.item: writing on the wall: how long each episode lasts
facts.text: It lasts less than a minute.

facts.item: writing on the wall: whether it is always there
facts.text: It comes and goes.

facts.item: writing on the wall: how often
facts.text: It has happened three to four times since yesterday.

facts.item: writing on the wall: with your eyes shut
facts.text: Occasionally I see it even when my eyes are shut.

facts.item: writing on the wall: what makes it go away
facts.text: Nothing makes it go away.

facts.item: writing on the wall: what makes it come more often
facts.text: Nothing makes it appear more often.
I feel as though I hear strange voices when I see the writing.
I can't understand them; the voices seem distant.

facts.item: feeling controlled by someone or something
facts.text: I don't feel like I'm being controlled.

facts.item: voices or writing telling you to harm someone
aliases: commands to hurt yourself or others
facts.text: The voices and the writing don't tell me to hurt myself or anyone else.
I've never had thoughts of harming myself.
I've never had thoughts of harming anyone else.
I haven't had any headaches.
My vision hasn't changed, and I haven't lost any vision.
My hearing hasn't gotten worse.
My sleep habits haven't changed.

facts.item: trouble waking up in the morning
facts.text: Sometimes I find it difficult to wake up in the morning.

facts.item: falling asleep suddenly during the day
facts.text: I haven't noticed myself falling asleep suddenly during the day.
Sometimes I feel very sleepy during the day.
I haven't had a fever.
My weight hasn't changed.
My appetite hasn't changed.
I've never had anything like this before.

other_considerations.note: Visual and auditory hallucinations fit, but DSM-5 excludes this diagnosis after recent ingestion of a substance known to cause psychosis.

other_considerations.diagnosis: Psychosis secondary to a medical condition
other_considerations.note: Neurologic, endocrine, hepatic or renal disease can cause hallucinations, but nothing in the history suggests one.
Its hallucinations are hypnagogic or hypnopompic; he has some daytime sleepiness, but not enough to support the diagnosis.
Epileptic visual hallucinations usually last seconds; unlikely with no known seizure history.

x005: Implausible as written (diastolic above systolic), probably a typo for the doorway 140/80 mm Hg; kept as the source wording per v1. The gold exam finding repeats 'Hypertension (BP 140/180)'.

source_issues: Age conflict: the opening scenario says 21 years old; the raw Patient Description and the note HPI say 27. Demographics use the opening-scenario age (21), the age the examinee sees at the door; the patient may give 27 if asked.

Blood pressure conflict: doorway BP 140/80 mm Hg; the note exam (e002) and the gold exam finding give 'BP 140/180', which is implausible (diastolic above systolic) and probably a typo. Both kept as written (x001 doorway, x005 'blood pressure on recheck').

Many answers are generic templates ('No changes.', 'No, there isn't.') that do not fit their questions grammatically (p007, p008, p010, p011, p013, p015-p017, p019, p022-p027, p030, p032, p036, p039). For p024 (medications), p025 (past medical history) and p027 (surgery) 'No changes.' does not actually answer the question; read as none and flagged. The note copies the artifact ('Medications: No changes.', 'PMH: No changes.').

Gold lists 'Delusions' for both diagnoses; the script never elicits a delusion (p015 denies feeling controlled). Only the note ('he thinks he might be getting instructions from them') and the SP's challenging question support it.
Gold 'Does not associate drug use with presentation' is not stated anywhere in the script.
The note says he used drugs '1 day before these events', but the script dates both the last drug use and the onset of the writing to yesterday.
Note-only items not asked in the script: no appetite change, no seizures, no previous similar episodes (from-note facts f026, f030, f027).
The raw Entrance/Reflective Listening checklist contains stray text ('495.', a sentence about capitalizing 'SP'); not patient content.
Challenging question has a doubled opening quotation mark in the source; cleaned in extras.
notes: Template negatives were read as plain 'No' answers; each one where the wording does not fit is flagged on the fact.
p017 is split into thoughts of harming himself (f015) and thoughts of harming others (f016); p009 into recent life changes (f048) and stress (f049).
p020 and p021 are mixed answers: the denial (no change in sleep habits f020; no sudden falling asleep f022) is absent, the added complaint (hard to wake up f021; daytime sleepiness f023) is present.
Drugs are recorded in the patient's words ('angel dust', 'Ecstasy'); the note's PCP/MDMA labels are not copied.
leakage: angel dust use (f039) is the key clue for the rank-1 diagnosis but is legitimate history and does not name the diagnosis, so it is not listed.

'Sit up in the bed' and 'staring at the wall' are kept as acting notes only (demeanor, not an examination finding), following the worked example, which keeps 'exhibit pain' and 'exhibit difficulty breathing' as acting notes.
Reviewer edit: age set to the opening-scenario value (21) for consistency with the other cases with age conflicts (028, 033).
20 template answers (No changes., No, there isn't., Not really.) checked against the June-2024 release: all are plain denials there; 22 facts confirmed.
